# Globally critical caps can violate original KKT-row residual-root Jensen

This is an exact obstruction to an unconditional proposed row inequality,
not a counterexample to OC. The actual convex source has a complete lattice
base, every fiber is strictly below the total mass divided by the occupied
parity count, the source is its unique deepest point, and the row is exactly
the absorbing-chain coupling of an attained residual-program KKT system.
EVERY globally critical cap through that source violates the same row
inequality. In particular, optimizing the critical cap menu does not repair
this row. The source remains strictly above the OC threshold.

The exact all-halfspace depth input is the proved theorem in
`candidate 1d1be0b22c707856`, Sections1–3,7;
its independent audit is
`unshared historical review/context (not an accepted premise)`.
The finite KKT-to-coupling definitions are in
`candidate 99d50c87eb055f05`.

## 1. Actual full-dimensional convex source

Let d>=2, let T be a d-simplex of volume one with one vertex at the origin,
and let lambda_0,...,lambda_d be its barycentric coordinates. Put

    gamma=(d/(d+1))^d, b=1/(d+1), c=(1-gamma)^(1/d).

Choose an integer n>=2 satisfying

    c<n/(n+1).                                             (1)

Put v_-=(-1,...,-1), v_+=(1,...,1), and

    P={0,1}^n union {v_-}.

At every cube vertex place T. At v_- place A=epsilon T, where
0<a:=epsilon^d<rho_d, with rho_d>0 the explicit proved simplex-profile
constant in the cited exact-depth theorem. Take the actual lifted convex
hull C of these bodies in R^n times R^d.

Its projection has exactly the integer points P. Indeed its coordinates
lie in [-1,1]. Any integer point outside the cube has a coordinate -1;
in a convex representation this forces all weight onto v_-, since every
cube vertex has that coordinate at least zero. Each cube fiber is exactly
T because all continuous generators lie in T and that base already has T.
The exposed fiber at v_- is exactly A. The body contains [0,1]^n times T,
so is full dimensional. Every integer fiber has positive d-volume.

There are k=2^n occupied parity classes; v_- has the same parity as v_+.
The total mixed mass and maximum fiber volume are

    M=2^n+a,       max_z V_z=1<M/k=1+a/2^n.                (2)

The cited exact-depth theorem, or its restriction to the actual triple
v_-,0,v_+ followed by the explicit upper caps below, gives the UNIQUE
deepest mixed-integer point (0,g), where g is the centroid of T, with
raw depth

    Q=gamma+a.                                             (3)

This is strictly above the sharp OC target:

    Q-gamma M/k=a(1-gamma/2^n)>0.                          (4)

The gap tends to zero as a tends to zero.

Condition(1) is available in every continuous dimension. For example
n=3d works: Bernoulli gives
(n/(n+1))^d>1-d/(n+1)>2/3, whereas gamma>1/3. For the latter,
(1+1/d)^d<sum_(j>=0)1/j!<3, where the last strict inequality follows by
bounding j!>=2^(j-1) for j>=2, strictly for j>=3. Thus
(n/(n+1))^d>1-gamma. The smaller pair n=3,d=2 will give a rational
coordinate certificate in Section6.

## 2. A finite genuine cap cover with budgets at most Q

Write delta_0(z)=sum_j z_j. For every simplex index i take

    H_i={lambda_i(x)-2 delta_0(z)>=b}.                     (5)

At base0 this is the canonical centroid cap of volume gamma. At v_-
it captures all A. At every nonzero cube base it is strictly empty.
Thus each H_i has exact mass Q and is globally critical at (0,g).

For each nonzero cube vertex w put

    delta_w(z)=(n+1) sum_(j:w_j=1)(1-z_j)
                              +sum_(j:w_j=0)z_j,
    G_(w,i)={lambda_i(x)-2 delta_w(z)>=b}.                 (6)

The function delta_w vanishes at w and is at least one at every other
cube vertex. If r is the number of ones in w, then
delta_w(v_-)=(2n+3)r-n>=n+3>0. Consequently each G_(w,i) isolates the
canonical cap at its own cube fiber, has mass gamma, and excludes every
other fiber. At every cube fiber the canonical caps cover T, because
sum_i lambda_i=1. The H_i also cover all A. Hence(5)–(6) are a finite
cover by original closed ambient halfspaces with budgets at most Q.

For the one-cap residual program, define

    e_z=min_F |C_z intersect F^c|^(1/d),                   (7)

where F ranges over this finite cover. Hyperplanes have zero d-volume,
so strict complements in(7) have the indicated volume roots. The exact
obstacles are

    e_(v_-)=0,              e_z=c for every cube vertex.  (8)

## 3. Unique convex-threshold optimum and exact KKT multipliers

The sampled convex-threshold program is

    minimize R=sum_z h_z^d,
    h_z>=e_z,
    h_y>=h_z+g_z dot(y-z) for all distinct z,y in P.       (9)

Its UNIQUE optimal sampled values are h_z=c for every z, and

    R=(2^n+1)c^d.                                        (10)

To see this without a solver, use 0=(v_-+v_+)/2. Convexity gives
h_(v_-)+h_(v_+)>=2h_0>=2c. Convexity of the dth power on nonnegative
numbers gives h_(v_-)^d+h_(v_+)^d>=2c^d. Each of the remaining 2^n-1
cube values is at least c. These bounds sum to(10), which h identically c
attains with all support slopes g_z=0. Equality in the power inequality
and in all remaining obstacle bounds forces every value to be c.

Put s=d c^(d-1)>0. Let e_1,...,e_n denote the coordinate unit vectors.
Choose the nonzero convexity multipliers

    mu_(0,v_-)=s,       mu_(0,e_j)=s for j=1,...,n,        (11)

and no others. The source moment equation is exact:
v_-+sum_j e_j=0. Set

    lambda_0=(n+2)s,
    lambda_(v_-)=lambda_(e_j)=0,
    lambda_w=s for every other cube vertex w.             (12)

These are the full KKT multipliers for(9). Every support constraint
is tight. Every positive lambda is at an obstacle contact. The
stationarity equations lambda=s+out-in hold at the source, its n+1
destinations, and all remaining bases separately. Thus this is an exact
KKT certificate, not merely a feasible barycentric row.

## 4. The canonical terminal coupling and strict failure

In the absorbing-chain formula a_z=s+out_z,
T_zy=mu_zy/a_z, D_zz=s/a_z, pi=diag(lambda)(I-T)^(-1)D,
only the source has outgoing edges. Its self-absorption probability is
1/(n+2), and each of its n+1 outgoing transitions has the same
probability and is immediately absorbed. Therefore the formula gives

    pi_(0,y)=s for y in {0,v_-,e_1,...,e_n},
    pi_(w,w)=s for all other cube vertices w,              (13)

and all remaining entries zero. Every column sums to s, every row sums
to its lambda in(12), and each row has the required base barycenter.
The normalized terminal row at the positive active source0 is precisely
the uniform law on the n+2 displayed destinations.

Fix any H_i from(5), and define its ORIGINAL residual-root function on
the actual integer fibers by

    f_i(z)=|C_z intersect H_i^c|^(1/d).

On this row its values are

    f_i(v_-)=0,       f_i(0)=c,       f_i(e_j)=1.          (14)

In particular H_i attains the residual obstacle at the source, is
globally critical there, and its source residual is positive. Nevertheless

    sum_y [pi_(0,y)/lambda_0] f_i(y)
      =(c+n)/(n+2)>c=f_i(0),                             (15)

with gap [n-(n+1)c]/(n+2)>0 by(1). This uses the ORIGINAL terminal
row and actual residual roots. No geometric stopping, altered row,
projective normalization, or root-to-volume passage is involved.

## 5. Every critical cap has the same failure

In fact all globally critical halfspaces through (0,g), up to positive
rescaling of their defining inequalities, are exactly

    F_(i,beta)={lambda_i(x)+beta dot z>=b},
    beta_j<=-(1-b)=-d/(d+1) for every j.                 (16)

For proof restrict a through-point cap to the actual triple
v_-,0,v_+. The exact-depth profile proof bounds the triple mass below by
Q. If the full cap has mass Q, it has equality on this triple and zero
volume on every other cube fiber. A cap with zero continuous normal
contains the entire middle fiber and at least one endpoint of this
triple, so has mass at least1+a>Q and cannot be critical.
For a nonzero continuous normal u, the cited proof has normalized
profile quantities f(u),q(u) satisfying

    f(u)>=gamma,    f(u)-gamma+q(u)>=rho_d>a,
    triple mass>=f(u)+min(a,q(u)).                       (17)

If q(u)<a, the triple mass exceeds Q strictly. Otherwise equality forces
f(u)=gamma; the ordinary simplex equality classification makes u a
canonical direction lambda_i. Its through-point equation is then the
one in(16). At each unit vertex e_j, zero cap volume on T is equivalent
to b-beta_j>=1, proving the coefficient inequalities. Conversely those
inequalities make every nonzero cube trace have zero d-volume, while
the v_- threshold is b+sum_j beta_j<=b-n(1-b)<0. They therefore capture
all A and the own canonical cap, giving exact mass Q.

At equality beta_j=-(1-b), the trace at e_j can be its canonical vertex;
it has zero d-volume but need not be the empty set. This has no effect
on(14). Thus EVERY cap in the full critical menu has the same row
residuals and strict failure(15).

Adjoining any such cap to the original finite cover leaves(8), the
unique optimum, all KKT data, and the original cover intact. One may
also replace H_i by a member of(16) having the SAME canonical direction:
the source canonical cover remains, A is still fully captured, and the
other cube fibers remain covered by(6). We do not infer coverage after
discarding an original cap and changing its canonical direction.

## 6. Smallest displayed rational-coordinate instance

Take d=2,n=3,

    T=conv{(0,0),(1,0),(0,2)}, epsilon=1/10,
    a=1/100, gamma=4/9, c=sqrt5/3.

The area of T is one. The profile criterion is valid because
a<rho_2=2(sqrt10-3)/9; equivalently
(3+9/200)^2<10, an exact rational inequality. Condition(1) is
c<3/4, equivalent to80<81. The values are

    Q=409/900, M=801/100, k=8,
    Q-gamma M/k=17/1800,
    R=9c^2=5,
    row gap=(9-4sqrt5)/15>0.                             (18)

All vertices and cap inequalities are rational. Only the exact
square-root residual heights and their scaled KKT multipliers are
irrational. The verifier
`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_globally_critical_original_kkt_row_counterexample_simplex_chains.py`
checks the finite base/parity data, cap isolation, normalized KKT
equations, terminal coupling, rational constants and strict inequalities.
The all-normal depth and menu arguments above are proofs, not outcomes
of a finite direction screen.

## 7. Scope

The unconditional original-row root inequality is false even with all
the following premises together: actual convex fiber inclusions, complete
lattice base, positive full-dimensional fibers, strict nonheaviness,
an attained convex-residual optimizer, a positive active KKT source at
the unique deepest point, an actual globally critical active cap, and
optimization over its entire globally critical cap menu.

This counterexample is strictly above OC. It does not refute an argument
which uses a BELOW-target assumption in an essential additional way,
nor a selection of DIFFERENT valid KKT multipliers. It does refute any
claim of the proposed inequality for every valid original KKT row under
the listed unconditional premises.
